questions.q: For areal data like census tracts, why is analyzing the arrangement of the locations themselves not useful?
options: The boundaries are arbitrarily defined, so the exact locations aren't meaningful; the values are
Tracts are always the same size
questions.why: With areal data and marked points, the question is how the values vary across space, which is what spatial autocorrelation measures.

questions.q: How should you choose a neighborhood definition?
options: Base it on a hypothesis about the process causing autocorrelation and on your study goals, then check how sensitive results are
Pick whichever gives the highest Moran's I
questions.why: The reading calls it more art than science. Running the analysis with several definitions shows whether the results are robust.

questions.q: Two tracts touch only at a single corner point. They are neighbors under...
questions.why: Queen's case counts any touching. Rook's case requires sharing more than a single point.

questions.q: Why can't you use topological neighborhoods for marked point data?
options: Points are always too far apart
questions.why: Topology depends on shared boundaries. For points, use distance-based or k-nearest neighborhoods.

questions.q: A dataset has a dense city and very sparse rural areas. Which neighborhood definition guarantees every feature the same number of neighbors?
questions.why: K-nearest neighbors picks the k closest features no matter how far away they are, so sparse areas still get neighbors.

questions.q: A Moran's I of 0.59 for median household income suggests...
questions.why: Positive I means similar values cluster. You still need a significance test, because chance alone can create structure.

options: high and low values are interspersed (negative autocorrelation)
questions.why: Negative I means neighbors tend to differ, like a checkerboard.

questions.q: What does LISA add that global Moran's I does not?
options: A single number for the whole map
A statistic for each location, showing where significant clusters and outliers are
questions.why: Global Moran's I summarizes the whole dataset. LISA maps local clusters (HH, LL) and outliers (HL, LH).

questions.q: In a LISA map, a high-income tract surrounded by low-income tracts is labeled...
questions.why: The first label is the location's own value and the second is its neighbors'. High-Low is a spatial outlier.

questions.q: How do you know you need a spatial regression model?
options: The residuals from a regular regression are spatially autocorrelated
questions.why: Regression requires independent residuals. If the residuals show autocorrelation, a spatial model is needed.

questions.q: Housing prices that spill over into neighboring areas (a diffusion process) fit best with...
questions.why: The lag model puts neighbors' outcomes (Wy) into the equation, which matches contagion or spillover: second-order structure.

questions.q: Spatial dependence that comes from omitted variables that vary smoothly over space fits best with...
questions.why: The error model puts the spatial structure in the error term, representing unobserved processes: first-order structure.
